data.title: Trump to Host Second Memecoin Dinner Tonight With TRUMP Down 99% From Peak
data.description: Trump is set to host a second dinner tonight for 185 top holders of his Official Trump (TRUMP) memecoin in Northern Virginia. TRUMP traded at $0.8950 Sunday, down 98.8% from its $73.43 peak in January 2025, according to The Block. Floyd Mayweather, Kevin O’Leary and Tristan Thompson are scheduled guests. Eight senators urged the White House to disclose attendees, calling the event a potential pay-to-play scheme; the CFTC reportedly backed off an inquiry into possible fraud involving TRUMP. Trump collected at least $636 million in transaction and licensing fees last year, while buyers lost a combined $3.81 billion through the end of June.

data.title: China, Korea and Taiwan Prepare Stock Rescues Ahead of Monday as S&P 500 Extends Losses
data.description:
China, Korea and Taiwan moved to support their stock markets ahead of Monday as the S&P 500 entered the session on a seven-day losing streak, its longest since February 2020. South Korea prepared a $7.3 billion stabilization fund, China will lower minimum margin requirements to 80% from 100% starting November 30, and Taiwan restricted short selling below the previous day’s close, according to BeInCrypto. South Korea’s finance minister called an emergency meeting with the central bank chief and three regulators on Sunday to try to prevent a “Black Monday.” China’s changes are expected to free up 400 billion yuan for stock purchases. Taiwan’s state fund has been buying shares since November 6, but the market still recorded its worst week since 1991.

The moves matter to Wall Street because Asian and U.S. markets are linked by the AI chip trade. Nvidia fell 14% on Friday, while AMD’s five-day decline exceeded 24%. Trend-following computer-driven funds sold $57 billion in stocks over a month; Goldman Sachs models project another $28.6 billion in sales if prices rise and $80.6 billion if they fall. JPMorgan Asset Management’s David Kelly called the selloff “not a fatal illness,” noting that the S&P 500 rose in the three months after 17 of 22 corrections since 1980, although five of 14 similar declines since 1983 became bear markets. Goldman said a softer Federal Reserve could mark a bottom, while traders priced a 91.4% chance of a December rate hike. U.S. futures reopen at 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, with Seoul markets opening an hour later.

data.title: STOCKS | Nasdaq 100 Approaches Bear Market as Dip Buyers Hold Back

data.description: OpenAI’s chief scientist proposed that AI companies agree to limit development of increasingly powerful models until researchers have better ways to understand and monitor their behavior, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Stocks' Retreat Rattles Bond Market's Favored Bet on Fed Hikes
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Wall Street is converging on a favored bond-market trade that bets the Federal Reserve will continue its push to tame inflation, even as falling stocks darken the economic outlook.

data.title: Fusionist Attack-Related Minting, Tornado and Cross-Chain Bridge Addresses Disclosed
data.description: Addresses linked to the Fusionist attack, including the attacker’s minting address, a Tornado router contract and the exploited cross-chain bridge, have been disclosed. According to Odaily, Onchain Lens identified the attacker’s minting address and a third address as 0x1029...e12c5, the second wallet as 0xb335...019b5, the Tornado router contract as 0xB6f0...01703, its sender as 0xFF85...0CFB, and the exploited bridge contract as 0x9d06...5915.

data.title: Blur Disables Contract Upgrades, Removing an ETH Recovery Route
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, NFT marketplace aggregator Blur has disabled contract upgrades, removing a route for recovering ETH by upgrading contracts. Developer Quit said 545.6 ETH is spread across 315 contracts with no direct withdrawal path. Withdrawals from regular wallets remain available.

data.title: STOCKS | Goldman Traders See US Selloff as Buying Opportunity, Warn of Positioning Risks
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s trading desk says last week’s selloff created an attractive opportunity to buy US stocks. The bank cautions that investor positioning remains elevated, and the broader capitulation it says is needed for a meaningful rally may be missing.

data.title: Eric Trump-Backed Foundation Future Industries Ends Employee Health Benefits Amid Cash Crunch
data.description: According to CNBC, employees at Eric Trump-backed robotics startup Foundation Future Industries were told their health benefits through Rippling had been terminated retroactive to October. A staff memo said workers would be offered COBRA coverage for November, and the company said it would reimburse premiums and was onboarding a new benefits provider. Rippling said Foundation had failed to meet its payroll and benefits obligations for multiple months. Employees were last paid on Oct. 15 and face a third straight pay cycle without income as another scheduled payday approaches on Nov. 30. Foundation has sought a bridge loan while awaiting a possible $150 million investment from South Korean conglomerate Base Group as early as December or January; Base said the investment was under consideration, but funding has not been finalized.

data.title: Solana Foundation Says Alpenglow Upgrade Set for Mid-October to Make Technology Faster, Cheaper and More Resilient
data.description: Solana Foundation Chief Strategy Officer Rachel Conlan said Alpenglow is scheduled for a core upgrade in mid-October that will make the technology faster, cheaper and more resilient. According to Odaily, Solana said in a post on X that representatives from Morgan Stanley, BNY Mellon and DTCC attended Breakpoint; Conlan also said the century-old financial industry is being reimagined.
